clue.text: Noisy display of anger with cutlery being thrown around

definitions.text: Noisy display of anger with cutlery being thrown around

parts.words: Noisy display of anger with cutlery being thrown around
parts.note: pictures a furious row with knives and forks flying, the figurative name for an angry outburst that is also a literal noisy pyrotechnic show

explanation.surface: A domestic row escalates until the cutlery starts flying across the room.
explanation.definitionFit: An angry outburst is figuratively called this, after the bangs and flashes of a pyrotechnic display.

clue.text: Ditch openings of foreign operas; Schwarzkopf sings English

indicators.note: openings are the starting letters, so the first letter of each of the next four words is taken

explanation.surface: The great soprano Elisabeth Schwarzkopf opens a series of foreign operas sung in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' sits apart from the opera picture; it is the definition, and the semicolon hides that the openings run on through 'Schwarzkopf sings'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fosse is a ditch or moat, especially one dug as a defence.

clue.text: You have to pay before you get it

definitions.text: You have to pay before you get it

parts.words: You have to pay before you get it
parts.note: sounds like a grumble about prepayment, but describes the slip a shop hands over only once money has changed hands

explanation.surface: A grumble about having to pay up front for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A proof of purchase is issued only after payment has been made, so payment always comes first.

clue.text: Stinger used to be soft

parts.note: was is the past tense of to be, meaning used to be
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Something that stings was once gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: This striped insect is a classic example of a creature with a sting.

clue.text: Weak thing — buck up!

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a buck is a male deer

explanation.surface: A rallying cry telling a feeble person to pull themselves together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buck up!' reads as encouragement, but buck is a male DEER and 'up' turns it over, giving REED.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender marsh plant that bends in the wind is proverbially a symbol of weakness, as in 'a broken reed'.

clue.text: Saw about Italian given over to science fiction filling a need

indicators.note: about means the saying is placed around the other letters

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb

indicators.note: given over means turned over, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: IT is a common abbreviation for Italian, as in vermouth

explanation.surface: An Italian proverb is adapted for a science-fiction story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the cutting tool or a verb, but it is an old proverb; 'given over' turns the Italian abbreviation round before 'about' wraps the proverb round it and the science fiction letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something satisfying fulfils a want, meeting a need fully.

clue.text: Covered animal's footprints without sign and direction

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so pad goes around the other letters

parts.note: pad can mean the paw of an animal or the track it leaves
V is the victory sign made with two fingers
E is the compass direction east

explanation.surface: An animal's tracks appear but with no sign of which way it went.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: PAD wraps round V and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A road that is paved has been covered with a hard surface such as stones or asphalt.

clue.text: Source of caper around potential hot spot

indicators.note: around means prance is placed round the other word

parts.note: to caper is to prance or leap about playfully
an oven is a place that can become very hot

explanation.surface: A prank or caper set in a potentially dangerous hot place.
explanation.definitionFit: Provenance is the origin or place where something comes from, so a synonym for source.

clue.text: Art theory, somewhat clever, is moving

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An artistic theory that is rather clever is said to be emotionally moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Verismo is the doctrine of realism in art and especially Italian opera, an artistic theory.

clue.text: Utterly blue Conservatives

parts.note: blue means feeling low or down
the political right means conservatives

explanation.surface: A remark that the Conservatives are blue through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the Conservative Party's colour, so 'blue Conservatives' reads as one picture, but blue is DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright as an adverb means thoroughly or completely, the same as utterly.

clue.text: Abandoned cur shows sore, wet at parting

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or unrestrained, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A dog left behind displays a wet wound as its owner leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet says 'Parting is such sweet sorrow' in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, so the phrase is what is felt at parting.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Juliet describes the feeling of saying goodbye with this phrase, so it names what one feels at parting.

clue.text: Dangerous to be around

indicators.note: around means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: A warning that it is risky to hang about here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wicked or harmful is a danger, so the adjective can stand for dangerous.

clue.text: Loss adjuster gets topless girls endlessly angry

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed from the word for girls

parts.note: lasses are girls

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off the word for angry

parts.note: sore means angry, as in feeling sore

explanation.surface: An insurance man meets some topless girls who are furious with him.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance assessor values damage and losses, which is the job of a loss adjuster.

clue.text: For example, Leo (novelist) requires publiciser

parts.note: Leo is an example of a star sign of the zodiac
a novelist is a writer

explanation.surface: A novelist named Leo needs someone to publicise his books.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo reads as a novelist's first name (Tolstoy), but it is a zodiac SIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter of shop signs and advertising boards publicises businesses.

clue.text: Two sovereigns delivered into her hand

indicators.note: delivered into means put inside

parts.note: her points to a woman
R stands for rex, Latin for king, one sovereign
a king is the second sovereign

explanation.surface: Two gold coins are handed over to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Sovereigns look like gold coins, but here they are two rulers, the Latin rex abbreviated and the full English word, both put into a woman, the 'her' of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand, so a working man.

clue.text: Dull edge on yuppie's first marriage

parts.note: matt or mat means dull, not shiny
a rim is an edge

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of yuppie is taken

explanation.surface: A dull life on the margins is a young professional's first marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Matrimony is the formal word for the state of being married.

clue.text: Head of family's armchair fitting to a T

indicators.note: fitting is read as fitting together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The head of the family's armchair suits them perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a T' reads as 'exactly', but the T is added to ARMCHAIR before 'fitting' rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is a woman who heads a family, so the word stands for head of the family.

clue.text: The way to Tipperary — in company

definitions.meaning: from the song It's a Long Way to Tipperary, where the way is described as a long one

explanation.surface: A First World War marching song sung together by soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tipperary is an Irish county; the old British army song says it is a long way there.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title calls the way to Tipperary a long one, and the word also means in company with someone.

clue.text: Keepsake for a man

parts.note: to can mean for, as in a gift to someone
Ken is a man's name

explanation.surface: A memento intended for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a small keepsake or memento.

clue.text: An oddity about belonging to up to fifty relatives in America

indicators.note: about means kink goes around the other letters

parts.note: a kink is a quirk or oddity

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: in American time-telling ten of five means ten to five, so to gives of
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A strange fact about having up to fifty relatives in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the American 'of' (as in ten of five for ten to five). 'in America' marks this as the US form of the word for relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinfolk is the American form of kinsfolk, meaning one's relatives.

clue.text: Old art of ruling with Billie Jean's service in court

parts.note: Billie Jean King was a famous tennis champion
her service, or serve, on the tennis court was her craft or skill

explanation.surface: Billie Jean King's serve on court is an old art.
explanation.walkthrough: Court looks like a royal court, fitting the ruling, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingcraft is the archaic term for the skill of ruling as a monarch.

clue.text: Capsule big enough to get Oxford University inside

indicators.note: inside means the university letters go within the other word

parts.note: ample means big enough, plentiful

explanation.surface: A capsule large enough to hold Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampoule is a small sealed glass vial holding a dose, a kind of capsule.

clue.text: Unaware of soldier's return, girl has discontented night

indicators.note: return means the letters are turned back

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
Nora is a girl's name

indicators.note: discontented means the contents are removed, leaving the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A girl spends a restless night, not knowing her soldier is coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant means lacking knowledge, so unaware of something.

clue.text: Footwear altercation

definitions.meaning: a cloth gaiter covering the ankle and shoe

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a short ankle gaiter and a minor quarrel.

clue.text: Contract to stand

definitions.meaning: to negotiate terms, to deal with
to pay for someone, as in stand a round of drinks

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to negotiate a deal and to pay for someone else's entertainment.

clue.text: Roger included in appeal to composer

indicators.note: included in means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: to beg is to appeal
R stands for roger, message received, in radio signalling

explanation.surface: Roger makes a plea to a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger looks like a name, but is R from radio talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: One boy brought up to be an artist

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means the letters are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: One boy is raised to become an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' looks like upbringing; it turns I plus LAD over.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dali was a Spanish surrealist painter.

clue.text: Short jumper for secretary, showing hesitation in mellow 22°C

parts.note: roo is the short form of kangaroo, a jumper

indicators.note: in means the secretary and hesitation go inside the word for mellow

parts.note: mature means mellow, as in wine or cheese
a temp is a temporary secretary
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A temp in a short sweater dithers in a mellow warm office.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper looks like a sweater (British for jumper) but is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal indoor warmth is about twenty-two degrees Celsius, the usual figure for comfortable indoor conditions.

clue.text: Country walker finds ex-president taking time out

indicators.note: taking means taking in, one piece holding another
out means the time letters are on the outside

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour, a time
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A rambler bumps into a former president on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time out' reads as a break, but HR (hour) goes outside IKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker is someone who walks long distances in the countryside.

clue.text: Book discovered in place of note in dressing gown — careless!

indicators.note: in place of means one piece replaces another

parts.note: a negligee is a light dressing gown
E is a musical note
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A book is found hidden in a dressing gown pocket by someone careless.
explanation.walkthrough: NT replaces the final E of NEGLIGEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means failing to take proper care, so careless.
